name: Put
summary: 17th-century English 3-card trick-taking game where 3 is high and players may risk everything on a "Put".
rules_text: Use 52 cards ranking 3-2-A-K-Q-J-10-9-8-7-6-5-4, no trumps. Players ante to game score, 5 or 7 points to win match. Deal 3 cards each singly. Non-dealer leads. Any card may be played, no need to follow. Higher rank wins trick; equal ranks tie the trick and it belongs to none. Winner leads next, same leader after a tie. Winning 2 of 3 tricks scores 1 point, trick-and-tie scores none. Before a trick, holder may say "Put" to play for the whole game. If opponent folds, putter scores 1. If opponent says "I see it", the hand is played and winner of most tricks wins the whole game (5 or 7) not just 1. A player may also fold on seeing cards, conceding 1. Deal alternates.
rating_reason: Old English trick-taking bluffing game, Truc family, 2p strategic
